newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:
Spokesman Nico Wegter said Commission President Santer and Singapore Prime Minister Chok Tong Goh would be available for pictures and questions in the hall of the Breydel at 1500/1300 GMT on Tuesday.
Wegter also said he would brief journalists at 1730/1530 GMT on Jacques Santer's meeting with Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa from 1730/1530 GMT.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the Commission had lodged a complaint against Japan with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) because of restricted access to Japanese harbour facilities by a monopolistic government-related company.

Spokesman Jesper Jorgensen briefed on Tuesday's Environment Council in Luxembourg. He said it would be an orientation debate and that decision were expected for December. Discussions will focus on the auto-oil programme, the communication on waste strategy, the drinking water quality standards and the 1997 Kyoto international convention on climate change.

In answer to a question, Wegter said Commissioner Hans van den Broek regretted the recent killing of a Greek Cupriot by Turkish Cypriot forces as he regretted the other killings that took place before in both camps. Van den Broek called for an inquiry by competent authorities and said the search for a solution would continue. - - - - -

- Speech/96/247: Speech by Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro, EU/SADC Ministerial conference.
